races.name: John Bircham And Stephen "Jagger" Hayes Memorial Juvenile Maiden Hurdle Race (GBB Race)
Happy 80th Birthday Ted Hull Mares' Maiden Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Arfursgal
runners_data.note: Consistent mare with multiple Good-ground placings — her 0W2P sim-going record and hold-up style mean she needs others to do the work, though Anthony Honeyball's yard is firing at 2/2 over 14 days and she has the class to capitalise if the pace is genuinely searching.

runners_data.name: Ask Peter
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type who has placed twice on Good going but posted 0W2P in similar conditions across 15 runs; James Robottom takes off a useful 10lb, yet the raw form figures suggest converting late runs into wins has been an issue throughout his career.

runners_data.name: Diamond White
runners_data.note: Prominent mare with back-to-back Good-ground placed efforts at this sort of trip; Jonjo O'Neill Jr. is an astute pilot for a horse that travels well in mid-race, and her 0W1P sim-going record understates a consistent level of performance that could be rewarded in a truly run contest.

runners_data.name: Getmyfriend
runners_data.note: The standout on form among prominent types — one win from four on Good ground, Dan Skelton's string running at 6/21 over 14 days, and Harry Skelton in the saddle; the 5yo has already demonstrated she can win when handy and this pace shape is tailor-made for her profile.

runners_data.name: Crystal Jet
runners_data.note: Has won on Good ground and showed up well in bumper form; naturally a prominent racer, but with Steal A Glance, Diamond White and Getmyfriend ahead of it in the pecking order, securing that front-end berth will be harder than usual — the 0.93 style-fit tag reflects genuine positional risk rather than a lack of ability.

runners_data.name: Lundy View
runners_data.note: Three runs, three finishes of 6th or worse on Good, all at a similar trip; David Noonan takes the ride for Nigel Hawke, but the consistent lack of impact in identical conditions is a significant flag and she is likely to again be racing out of contention by the home turn.

runners_data.name: Steal A Glance
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in this field, free to roll along at her own pace under 5lb claimer Chad Bament — her recent form (5,9,3,7,2) is patchy and she has never won, but the uncontested lead on Good ground could flatter her through much of the contest before she is headed late.

runners_data.name: Take The Boat
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and genuinely prominent by nature with consistent Good-ground placed form (2,3,2), but displaced into a midfield mapping here because the front end is already occupied; Harry Bannister will struggle to slot her into the position that suits her best, and the positional compromise is a real cost to her chance.

races.paceDynamic: Steal A Glance is the lone confirmed front-runner and, ridden by a 5lb claimer in Chad Bament, is likely to bowl along at a sustainable gallop from the outset without any genuine rivals capable of burning it out of the saddle early. Diamond White and Getmyfriend are the authentic prominent horses who will sit just off the pace and exert pressure through the middle stages, though the field contains more pace-hungry types — Crystal Jet and Take The Boat are natural prominent racers who have been displaced into a midfield mapping because there simply is not room for all of them on the front end. With a single uncontested lead horse dictating an honest but not scorching tempo on Good ground over 2m1f, this race shape overwhelmingly favours the prominent-to-midfield profile that can travel smoothly into contention and pick off the leader from the second-last; true hold-up horses asking for a sustained late run face the least favourable conditions here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steal A Glance Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Steal A Glance bowls along unchallenged and sets a comfortable, measured gallop that suits horses racing prominently in its wake.
scenarios.body: Steal A Glance dictates every yard at a tempo it can sustain, and the principals best placed to challenge are those travelling prominently just behind — the first to reel it in from the second-last wins the day. Getmyfriend, with a win on Good over this sort of trip and Harry Skelton aboard, and Diamond White, placed twice on similar going, are perfectly positioned to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Quicken Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Diamond White and Getmyfriend press Steal A Glance from the outset, lifting the tempo and forcing a searching gallop from halfway.
scenarios.body: The pressure drains Steal A Glance turning for home and the two prominent challengers engage in their own battle up the straight, suiting the horse with the superior jumping and fitness. Getmyfriend's course-and-distance profile on Good ground and Jonjo O'Neill Jr.'s experience on Diamond White make both prime beneficiaries of this contested shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace genuinely hotts up through the middle stages and collapses the front-runners, creating a vacuum for those held off the pace.
scenarios.body: Ask Peter or Lundy View would need a thorough test to produce a meaningful late rattle from the back, but their form figures suggest they struggle to convert even when the scenario suits them. Arfursgal, the most class-laden hold-up type with Good-ground placed form at bigger trips, represents the best candidate if a true staying test emerges.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Disrupt
scenarios.trigger: If Crystal Jet or Take The Boat manage to assert their natural prominent position early, overcrowding the front and sparking a chaotic early gallop.
scenarios.body: A scrambled early pace with multiple heads in front could produce an uneven rhythm that unbalances the more polished jumpers and throws the race open to an unexpected result. Both Crystal Jet and Take The Boat carry the STYLE_FIT discount precisely because they are unlikely to secure that natural position, making this the least probable shape.

watchPoints.text: Steal A Glance: monitor whether Chad Bament (5lb claimer) allows the mare to stride on naturally or gets drawn into fighting for position — if she jumps cleanly and finds a clear lead, she could outrun her OR considerably longer than her win-free record suggests.

Crystal Jet and Take The Boat: watch at the start and first two hurdles to see whether either natural prominent type manages to push up and crowd the front end — if they do, the gallop could become ragged and upset the rhythm of the more polished performers.

Getmyfriend: her jumping fluency is pivotal — Harry Skelton needs her to travel smoothly just off the pace; any jumping error or loss of momentum in the back straight could cost her the ground she would normally gain effortlessly.

Arfursgal: 54 days since last run is the longest absence in the field — Anthony Honeyball runners are in good form, but watch for signs of ring-rustiness, particularly in how she travels in the early stages given she needs a strong pace to deliver her late effort.

Lundy View: consistent tail-ender on Good ground at this course — if she is again detached in rear by halfway, her presence is effectively irrelevant to the race shape and the tactical picture can be read purely through the front six.

races.name: Dick Oliver At Newton Abbot Races Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: It's A Breeze
runners_data.note: Paul Nicholls in excellent 1/1 14-day form, and this horse arrives just 6 days after a win over 21f on good ground — the step up to 2m5f on the same going looks well-suited; a genuine hold-up horse whose recent course-and-distance equivalent form reads better than the headline mark suggests, and the hood headgear is unchanged.

runners_data.name: The Gypsy Davey
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with a standout 14-of-15 runs on good or good-equivalent ground, giving enormous confidence in conditions here; trainer C Williams returns 1/6 in the 14-day window and the horse arrives fresh on 6 days' rest — the 2/21f/GOO run most recently underlines the current form.

runners_data.name: Chief Black Robe
runners_data.note: Fergal O'Brien sends this 10-year-old back after a 71-day break, and he is a natural rear-of-field operator who the crowded hold-up market forces into a more prominent midfield role — worth noting his three of four placed efforts in his history came on going softer than today, and the good ground here is a mild query.

runners_data.name: Chillhi
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with tongue-tie and cheekpieces fitted, trained in Ireland and making a run in Britain; the hold-up style is genuine but this horse is effectively forced closer to the pace than preferred in this shape, and a record showing 9th, P, 7th in recent outings including a fall code suggests reliability questions that compound the positional compromise.

runners_data.name: Flashy Boy
runners_data.note: Robbie Llewellyn's 9-year-old has zero wins or places on good ground across eight attempts — all his best form came on soft or softer — so today's going is a concrete concern regardless of running style; mapped to midfield out of natural rear-of-field position, the combination of going mismatch and style displacement makes this a hard horse to support.

runners_data.name: Watchoutitscookie
runners_data.note: Nigel Hawke's 8-year-old has a modest record — no wins in any of the 15 runs on comparable going — and the 42-day layoff adds a mild freshness question; a true hold-up type pushed into midfield, and a horse who has finished 7th, 11th in recent good-ground chases, so the redistribution exacerbates an already limited winning profile.

runners_data.name: Senor Diaz
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, Jimmy Frost trained and carrying just 142lbs, arriving on 53 days' rest with three of five career runs on good ground; the style-fit flag reflects the fact he will be racing far more prominently than most rivals, but in this race that is actually his natural position — his sole realistic scenario is controlling from the front and lasting home.

runners_data.name: Emberscombe
runners_data.note: Joe Tickle's 9-year-old arrives on a sharp 18-day turnaround after a 6th on good ground, and the trainer is in excellent 2/7 form in the 14-day window; a natural hold-up horse who is likely to secure one of the better midfield positions given the configuration of this field, and the placed form over 25f good ground in the hist gives trip confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Senor Diaz is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner chase over 2m5f on good ground at Newton Abbot, and with no rival likely to seriously challenge for the lead, he should dictate a controlled, honest gallop throughout — not a crawl, but a tempo set entirely on his own terms. The rest of the field is composed almost entirely of hold-up horses, meaning the pack will trail in his wake before the race ignites in the final circuit. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with proven finishing ability on good ground, particularly those who can travel smoothly through the race and produce a sustained late run — the longer 2m5f trip over fences rewards stamina and a clean jumping profile over raw pace. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Chief Black Robe, Chillhi, Flashy Boy, Watchoutitscookie, and Emberscombe are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield, and in practice it will be the most naturally prominent among them — most likely Chief Black Robe and Emberscombe — who actually secure the better-positioned midfield berths closest to Senor Diaz.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Senor Diaz Dictates Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Senor Diaz jumps well and sets an uncontested, measured gallop that leaves the hold-up field with too much to do in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Senor Diaz bowls along in front at a tempo that suits his jumping rhythm, and the hold-up pack — needing every one of the 2m5f — fail to reel him in before the line; good-ground form vindicates the front-runner.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Senor Diaz sets a strong enough pace that the genuine hold-up horses — those truly racing in their natural role — can unleash a meaningful late run to overhaul him.
scenarios.body: It's A Breeze and The Gypsy Davey, both true hold-up operators with solid good-ground form, track the pace patiently and use their stamina reserves to collar the leader approaching the last; the 2m5f distance amplifies the advantage of a well-judged waiting ride.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Improver Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed hold-up horses who take up midfield positions race more prominently than usual and capitalise on proximity to the pace at the business end.
scenarios.body: Chief Black Robe or Emberscombe, slotting into a handy midfield position closer than their natural style, benefit from seeing daylight early in the straight and grind out a winning challenge; the style-fit discount applies but the positional advantage in a thin field partially compensates.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart Chaotically
scenarios.trigger: If Senor Diaz makes a significant jumping error or capitulates, triggering a scramble among the reshuffled hold-up pack with no natural pace controller.
scenarios.body: A muddled tempo with the field bunched creates a tactical lottery over the final mile, favouring whoever jumps most fluently and travels best through the race rather than any defined pacing profile; at this point raw class and OR advantages for The Gypsy Davey and It's A Breeze give them the edge.

watchPoints.text: Watch Senor Diaz's jumping at the early fences — if he makes a significant error in the first mile he loses his controlling advantage entirely and the race opens up unpredictably for the crowded hold-up pack.

It's A Breeze is on a very quick 6-day turnaround; watch the pre-race market move — if Nicholls is confident the horse has fully recovered, the timing angle strengthens, but any drift could flag a fitness concern.

Chief Black Robe returns after 71 days off — watch whether he travels sweetly through the race; a fit, freshened horse could outrun his redistribution penalty, but a laboured jump or tired exit early signals the layoff has told.

With five or more hold-up horses compressed into midfield, watch for traffic problems on the home turn — horses racing out of their natural rhythm may lack the room or momentum to mount a clean challenge if the field bunches behind Senor Diaz approaching the straight.

Flashy Boy's going record (0W0P from 8 runs on good ground) is worth monitoring at the off — if conditions firm up any further, his chance shrinks further regardless of how the race is run tactically.

races.name: Brendon Soper Memorial Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Son Of Hypnos
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator for Ryan Chapman; 38 days off the track is worth noting, Jack Stenhouse claims 7lb which helps offset his 168lb burden, and his Good-ground form reads 3/16f and 7/16f — staying on rather than winning.|

runners_data.name: Ugo Bingo
runners_data.note: Back just six days after his last run, Brendan Powell takes the ride for Joe Tizzard whose yard is 0/3 over the past 14 days; goes well on Good ground (9 of 15 runs) but a hold-up style in a race likely to be run at a measured pace makes timing the challenge difficult.|

runners_data.name: Linden Lane
runners_data.note: Osian Radford claims 10lb and the trainer has been in decent form (1/6 T14); four placed efforts from seven Good-ground starts suggest consistent rather than brilliant, and the hold-up style suits a race with late drama more than a steady-tempo scenario.|

runners_data.name: Applejack Poet
runners_data.note: Barry John Murphy has three runners in this race and Applejack Poet carries top weight from the redistributed group — while his natural instinct is to race from behind, his recent Good-ground experience (all 15 runs) and OR of 87 make him the most dangerous of those forced to race out of position.|

runners_data.name: Makinbecon
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field and wears a tongue-strap; two wins from four Good-ground starts and a record of 1/20f/GOO in his last run show he can quicken over this type of trip — sole control of pace is a significant tactical weapon here.|

runners_data.name: Saucats
runners_data.note: Tongue-strap fitted and the most active trainer of the meeting (2/7 T14); his Good-ground record is exemplary (13/15 runs, 1W5P) and as the only other prominent-style horse he will look to park just behind Makinbecon — a position that maximises his chance in the dominant scenario.|

runners_data.name: Man Oh Man
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and is a true hold-up type by nature, though redistributed to a midfield mapping given the volume of hold-up horses; his most recent run was a second over 18f on Good ground (2/18f/GOO) and the 26-day break is not a worry, but Bryan Carver will need to find a way through.|

runners_data.name: Yanka Blue
runners_data.note: A fifth runner for the Barry John Murphy yard and genuinely a hold-up horse in style, shifted forward on the map because the rear is congested; his last start produced a second (2/18f/GOO) but his overall form suggests finding one or two too good rather than winning — lowest OR of the field at 77.|

runners_data.name: Mi Sueno
runners_data.note: Nick Scholfield sends out this 7-year-old 32 days after his last run; all five recent form runs have been over shorter (16f) and stepping up to 22f is an unknown — his hold-up style and natural reluctance to dominate make him reliant on the race falling perfectly, while the T14 rate of 2/9 offers mild trainer confidence.|

races.paceDynamic: Makinbecon is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rivals willing to take him on from the front, he should stride into an uncontested lead and control tempo from the outset on Good ground at Newton Abbot. Saucats is the only other prominent-style runner and will likely sit close behind Makinbecon in second or third, creating a small lead group with the rest of the field strung out behind. The pace is unlikely to be severe — one horse dictating on Good ground over 2m2½f sets up a falsely run affair where those at the front can conserve energy and quicken late from a position of comfort. This race shape strongly favours front-running and prominent horses who can control the race from the front — Makinbecon and Saucats are the obvious beneficiaries. The field contains more genuine hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear, with Applejack Poet, Man Oh Man, Yanka Blue, and Mi Sueno all redistributed to midfield — of these, Applejack Poet and Man Oh Man, with superior ORs and recent form, are most likely to push forward and genuinely secure a prominent position if they choose to.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Makinbecon Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Makinbecon leads without serious early pressure and dictates a measured tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Makinbecon sets the fractions to suit himself on Good ground, conserving enough energy to assert again from the last hurdle home; Saucats, sitting close in his slipstream, is ideally placed to mount a challenge but risks being outgunned by the leader's tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Saucats pushes up to challenge Makinbecon early, injecting more pace and turning this into a genuine two-horse battle from the front.
scenarios.body: A contested lead on Good ground still suits horses positioned at the front, but increases the risk of both front-runners tying up late; a well-positioned Applejack Poet or Linden Lane could then pick up the pieces from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Steady Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is so conservative that the hold-up horses can close the gap dramatically in the home straight.
scenarios.body: A truly pedestrian gallop compresses the field and allows the better-rated hold-up types racing from midfield to land a challenge entering the straight; Son Of Hypnos and Ugo Bingo have the class ceiling to capitalise if the race falls apart for the leaders late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Thins The Field
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or the trip catches out several runners and the race turns into a test of endurance and accuracy.
scenarios.body: Newton Abbot's tight track can punish those who make mistakes at hurdles, and a race of that nature would favour the most consistent jumper still travelling well late; Linden Lane's solid placed record at this sort of trip makes her a player in a contest decided by attrition.

watchPoints.text: Makinbecon leads entirely unchallenged — if Callum Pritchard is allowed to dictate a dawdle, he could steal a decisive advantage rounding the final bend that the hold-up horses simply cannot recover.
Saucats was only six days ago and wears a tongue-strap — watch whether Ben Godfrey elects to press Makinbecon early or ride conservatively, because that decision shapes the entire tempo of the race.

Applejack Poet, Man Oh Man, and Yanka Blue are all natural hold-up types compressed into midfield — monitor the first two furlongs for positioning scrimmages as horses compete for a realistic racing position.

Jack Stenhouse's 7lb claim on Son Of Hypnos reduces a significant weight burden, but the 38-day absence and a recent form string of 6P37-7 means he needs significant improvement on recent evidence to feature.

Barry John Murphy saddles three runners (Applejack Poet, Makinbecon, Yanka Blue) — team tactics could play a role, with Makinbecon's front-running role potentially setting up the race for stablemates if they can get close enough to benefit.

races.name: Zero To Exit Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Byzantium
runners_data.note: Paul Nicholls' 6yo has a win from five over similar Good-ground trips and goes fresh (53 days off) for a trainer in red-hot 14-day form (1/1); races with a tongue-tie and headgear, and the uncontested lead here is a significant tactical asset, though the STYLE_FIT flag suggests some caution if things don't unfold to plan.

runners_data.name: Time To Bite
runners_data.note: An 11yo veteran with seven wins and 10 placings from 15 similar-going runs, giving him outstanding credentials for Good ground over staying trips; prominent style suits this race shape neatly, the tongue-tie is retained, and 21 days since his last run leaves him fresh enough to be competitive at OR 111.

runners_data.name: Muskerry Rock
runners_data.note: Dan and Harry Skelton combine with a 7yo who won last time out at 26f on Good ground and has four wins or places from five recent similar-going starts; ran just six days ago which needs monitoring for any residual fatigue, but the stable operates at a high strike rate and this horse's hold-up style is genuinely suited to a race where leaders may weaken.

runners_data.name: Jager Time
runners_data.note: Fergal O'Brien's 7yo for daughter Fern (5lb claim) holds solid staying form — won at 25f on Good ground and placed in four of five recent outings at similar trips; genuine hold-up style means it needs leaders to fold, and the 26-day freshener is fine, though the trainer's 1/9 recent strike rate is modest.

runners_data.name: Juggernaut
runners_data.note: Anthony Honeyball's 7yo shows multiple placings in staying hurdles on Good ground and the trainer's 2/2 14-day form is a positive flag; prominent style is compatible with this race shape, though OR 100 and a 56-day break mean it needs to find improvement to seriously threaten the higher-rated pair up front.

runners_data.name: I Am Spider Man
runners_data.note: Barry John Murphy's 9yo has been consistently placing — five consecutive top-three finishes at this distance on Good — and was last seen 14 days ago; in reality a hold-up horse by nature, it has been pushed forward in the visual map because the rear of this field is unusually crowded with true closers, and the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) reflects that its optimal position may not be achievable here.

runners_data.name: Stavanger Rose
runners_data.note: Harriet Dickin's 6yo carries the lowest weight (143lbs) and lowest OR (85) in the field, with a form string of UF-640 suggesting fragility and a complete absence of placing form on Good ground (0W0P from five similar-going runs); a genuine hold-up type placed forward on the map due to congestion at the rear, the tongue-tie is retained but the overall profile is weak.

races.paceDynamic: Byzantium is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in this seven-runner field over 3m2½f at Newton Abbot, should establish a comfortable, pressure-free gallop from the outset. Time To Bite and Juggernaut will press from prominent positions, creating a steady but not searching early tempo on Good ground — functional enough to keep the field honest but unlikely to turn this into a true test of stamina from the front. The hold-up contingent — Muskerry Rock and Jager Time — will be held off the pace in the rear third, needing the leaders to tire sufficiently in the closing stages to mount a meaningful challenge. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or in a close-up position without burning energy early, then sustain their effort through the final circuit; true closers face a tougher ask unless the pace quickens materially in the middle stages. Note that I Am Spider Man and Stavanger Rose are genuine hold-up horses reassigned to midfield in the map — the rear of the field is more congested than the visual shape suggests, and Byzantium along with Time To Bite are the horses most likely to actually control the forward positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Byzantium Leads, Converts
scenarios.trigger: If Byzantium secures an uncontested lead and the pace remains controlled throughout, allowing it to dictate every yard.
scenarios.body: Byzantium, handled by Paddy Hanlon for the powerful Paul Nicholls yard (1/1 in 14-day strike rate), sets a sustainable gallop and simply outstays challengers from the front on Good ground it handles well (9/12 in similar going); Time To Bite is best placed to track and challenge but Byzantium's uncontested lead gives it a crucial energy advantage late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace from Byzantium is deceptively quick and the prominent horses tire, allowing hold-up types to come with a sweeping challenge from behind.
scenarios.body: Muskerry Rock, with Harry Skelton aboard and two wins from five in similar going, is ideally suited to a race where stamina is exposed late over this extended trip; Jager Time similarly boasts consistent placing form at this sort of distance and would benefit from leaders hitting a flat spot in the final half mile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Grind Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop quickens in the middle stages and the race becomes a genuine test of staying power, suiting a relentless prominent runner.
scenarios.body: Time To Bite's consistent Good-ground form (13/15 in similar going, 7 wins from 10 placings) and veteran's tactical nous at 11 years old gives it the edge if this develops into an honest slog; Juggernaut's multiple placings in similar staying contests show it handles this kind of attritional race well, and Anthony Honeyball's recent 2/2 strike rate is worth noting.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Favours Wildcard
scenarios.trigger: If early jumping errors or a false pace disrupts the field order and reshuffles running positions mid-race.
scenarios.body: I Am Spider Man, though a true hold-up horse placed into midfield by the race shape rather than its natural inclination, has placed four times in its last five runs at this trip on Good ground and could benefit from a muddled race where its consistency counts; Stavanger Rose is out of form and outrated but unpredictable enough to feature if the race falls apart.

watchPoints.text: Byzantium's uncontested lead is the hinge point of this race — if anything disrupts its rhythm at the early hurdles (jumping errors flagged by the hg:ht headgear combination), the entire race shape collapses and the pace advantage evaporates.

Muskerry Rock ran just six days ago; watch for any sign of below-par jumping or laboured movement in the preliminaries that might indicate the quick turnaround has left its mark on a horse that otherwise profiles as the most likely beneficiary of a late challenge.

I Am Spider Man and Stavanger Rose are both true hold-up horses compressed into midfield by the race shape — if they attempt to creep forward to find a more natural position, they risk spending energy out of role and compromising their late-race effectiveness.

Time To Bite's veteran profile (age 11, 21 days fresh, Good-ground specialist) means any deterioration in going — even within the "Good" band — is worth tracking; Newton Abbot's going has been consistent all card but ground conditions late in the day can change.

James Robottom (10lb claimer) rides Juggernaut for a trainer in strong recent form — a young rider aboard a staying type in a small field can sometimes produce an unexpectedly bold front-running or prominent display that unsettles the established order around Byzantium.

races.name: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: Premier Fantasy
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator for Nick Scholfield who has solid form on Good going (sim-going 3/3 placed), sits 7 years old and lightly campaigned recently; returns 30 days fresh, but finishing from the rear depends entirely on whether the solo pace from No More No is strong enough to set up a late run.

runners_data.name: No More No
runners_data.note: Four wins from five on Good ground over 24f underlines his affinity for today's conditions, and as the race's only natural front-runner he can dictate entirely on his own terms; trainer Lawney Hill has a blank 14-day record here, but Powell's handling of the horse (7/11 sim-going) is the key positive.

runners_data.name: Great d'Ange
runners_data.note: Tom Broughton (3lb claimer) takes the ride for Alexander Gibbons 16 days after his last run; a veteran of 10 years, his sim-going record is solid (14/15 runs on Good) but his recent form includes two pulled-up runs and a 9th, making reliability the primary concern over this marathon trip.

runners_data.name: Edgewell
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by nature — four wins on Good going and a strong 10/15 sim-going record — that Nick Scholfield's yard runs 9 days fresh, which is a brisk turnaround; the STYLE_FIT flag tempers his chance since racing from midfield rather than a true rearward pitch slightly compromises his best role.

runners_data.name: My Girl Katie
runners_data.note: Returns from a 323-day absence for Grace Harris (trainer 2/13 14-day), which is the single largest question mark in this field; two wins on Good at 26f-28f show she handles the trip and conditions when fit, and if the layoff hasn't blunted her, prominent racing could see her sit right behind the leader.

runners_data.name: Honey I'm Good
runners_data.note: Consistent placed form on Good going (sim-going 10/15, second twice at 26f) for Mrs C Williams, but a natural hold-up type pushed forward on the map due to the field's depth of closers; the STYLE_FIT flag is a mild discount and at OR=83 she needs things to fall perfectly for a prominent challenge.

runners_data.name: Mcgregors Charge
runners_data.note: Polly Gundry's eight-year-old has placed figures at 26f on Good in his history but carries recent form of 2PP7, with the pulled-up runs a durability flag at this extreme distance; mapped to midfield though naturally rearward, so Ben Godfrey will need to position him handier than ideal to get competitive.

runners_data.name: Testflight
runners_data.note: Tabitha Worsley partners this consistent but placed-only performer — four third-place finishes in sim-going races tells the story of a reliable stayer who rarely wins; at OR=76 and 142lbs, he needs an honest pace and a clear run from a prominent pitch but lacks the rating ceiling to trouble the principals.

races.paceDynamic: No More No is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no natural rival to push the pace, Brendan Powell can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop across this 3m2f trip on Good ground — a classic lone-leader scenario. My Girl Katie and Testflight will look to race prominently but neither carries the same front-running conviction, meaning No More No is likely to find himself in front without a fight and able to coast the early sections. The field behind is dominated by hold-up horses — Premier Fantasy, Great d'Ange, Edgewell, Honey I'm Good, and Mcgregors Charge are all natural rearward types, though Edgewell, Honey I'm Good, and Mcgregors Charge have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field cannot accommodate that many closers at the back simultaneously. With the pace owner uncontested and likely to travel comfortably, this race shape strongly favours a prominent or front-running profile — horses that can sit on No More No's quarters and produce a sustained challenge from two out, rather than hold-up horses who may find the gallop insufficiently strong to generate a finishing surge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: No More No Controls
scenarios.trigger: If No More No establishes an uncontested lead and sets a comfortable, measured gallop that fails to stretch the field early enough to tire him.
scenarios.body: No More No bowls along at his own pace through the first circuit, and with Good ground rewarding his sound jumping record (4 wins from 5 at 24f on Good), he has every chance to repel challengers from two out; his 7/11 sim-going record backs his claims here, and Powell is an able handler of front-runners at Newton Abbot.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Patient Tracking Pays
scenarios.trigger: If the true hold-up horses (Edgewell, Premier Fantasy) successfully time a run and the solo lead creates a strong-enough gallop in the final mile to expose No More No.
scenarios.body: Edgewell carries genuine class (OR=96, 4 wins on Good) and has won over this trip-profile before, while Premier Fantasy's hold-up style suits if pace is honest enough; both need No More No to set a punishing tempo, which is not guaranteed given he has no pacemaker company.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If My Girl Katie or Testflight tuck in directly behind No More No and produce a fresh challenge from the last fence after a prolonged lay-up trip.
scenarios.body: My Girl Katie returns from 323 days off and has two wins on Good going over similar distances, suggesting a fresh horse with natural prominent pace could sit comfortably on the leader's heels and sustain a run; Testflight's consistent placed form at 26f on Good (three third-placed finishes) makes her a reliable threat under this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Heap Closes
scenarios.trigger: If No More No sets a genuinely testing gallop that strings the field out and allows the true closers at the rear to pick off tired rivals.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on multiple hold-up horses — Honey I'm Good, Mcgregors Charge, Great d'Ange — racing in their true position and firing together, but the redistributed map placement signals the field has too many closers for all to find clear runs; on a steady pace, this shape is the least likely to materialise.

watchPoints.text: No More No — watch whether Brendan Powell elects to bowl along in front from flag-fall or is content to be taken on early; any pressure from My Girl Katie or Testflight in the first mile would fundamentally change the race shape.

My Girl Katie — a 323-day absence is a major unknown; watch how she moves in the parade ring and whether Ben Jones settles her immediately from a prominent position, as a fresh horse that over-races early could capitulate at the last fence.

Edgewell — running just 9 days after his last outing, watch for any sign of staleness or jumping errors under Harry Reed; a tired jumper over fences at Newton Abbot over 3m2f is a falls risk late in the race.

Great d'Ange — two DNF entries in his recent history and a 3lb claimer in the saddle at age 10 over this stamina-sapping trip; watch the early fences for any jumping hesitancy that might trigger another exit.

Mcgregors Charge — Ben Godfrey will need to place him closer than his natural instincts dictate; watch the first circuit to see whether he actually gets a prominent-midfield berth or drops to the rear, which would make his task near-impossible.
